Complainant police filed charge sheet against accused No.1 & 2 for the offences punishable under
sections 465, 468, 471, 420, 511, 201 r/w 34 of Ipc.
2. Brief facts of prosecution case are that :-
It
is the case of the prosecution that accused No.1 herein contacted CW-2 and promised her that he will apply for CM Relief Fund for the medical expenditure bared by CW-2.

Later after collecting CW-2's BPL card, Voter Id card and by colluding with accused No.2 got created fake medical bills by using the letter head of Sagar Hospital as if CW-2 underwent treatment for heart decease with fake IP number 183043 with Dr.Chandrashekar.
M.R. Further accused No.1 & 2 created fake discharge summary by forging the signature of Dr.Chandrashekar.
M.R. Later they applied for CM Relief Fund by using their medical records.
The Government has approved to sanction Rs.75,000/-.
When CW-1 sent the medical records to Sagar hospital to know that its genunity then he found that the said bills are fake bills.
Accordingly, he filed complaint and after the investigation the IO filed this charge sheet against the accused.
3. Accused No.1 & 2 have appeared before the court and they were enlarged on bail.
After filing of charge sheet, cognizance of above offences is taken and summons is issued.
Accused No.1 & 2 had appeared in pursuant summons.
Copies of charge sheet is furnished to accused u/s 207 of Cr.P.C and charge is framed.
Accused No.1 & 2 have not pleaded guilt of alleged offences and they have claimed to be tried.

6. Heard arguments of learned Sr.APP and learned counsel for accused.
Perused oral and documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution.
The following are findings to above points.

Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 7. Point No.1 :- In support of the case of prosecution examined PW-1 to 9 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 17. CW-6 examined as PW-1.

He being one of the Lab Technician at Sagar clinic deposed that the police conducted seizure mahazar in his presence at Sagar hospital and they obtained details of employees working in the said hospital.

Accordingly, he put signature on seizure mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.7.
8.
Further prosecution examined CW-9 as PW-2 and he deposed that Lakshmi is his wife and Raju is his relatives and Lakshmi had taken treatment in Punya hospital, Channapatna.
However he turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution.
9. Further prosecution examined CW-1 as PW-3.
He being complainant deposed that CW-2 had made application for CM relief fund for the expenditures on her treatment for Rs.3,60,000/-.
Accordingly, Hon'ble Minister sanctioned Rs.75,000/- to CW-2.
Later in order to know the genuinity of the said bills he sent the same to Sagar Hospital.
However the said hospital submitted report stating that CW-2 had never taken treatment in their hospital.
Further deposed that after receiving the reports he filed the complaint as per Ex.P.3.
Further he identified application made by CW-2 the same is marked as Ex.P.4.
Discharge summary, medical bills are marked as Ex.P.5 to 6.
Further chief of PW-1 deferred.
However, subsequently prosecution not examined the PW-1 and not tendered for cross examination.
Hence evidence of PW-1 is discharged on 14.02.2019.
10. Further prosecution examined CW-11 as PW-4.

He being the Doctor at Sagar hospital deposed that he do not know accused personally but he came to know that accused had created fake documents in the name of Sagar hospital to get the compensation from CM Relief Fund.
Accordingly, he has given statement before the IO.
11. Further CW-15 examined as PW-5.
He being one of the Investigating Officer deposed that he received file from CW-14.
Later handed over the same to CID as per the order of Police Commissioner.
12. Prosecution also examined CW-17 as PW6.
He being one of the Investigating Officer deposed that he received file from CW-16.

The said documents are furnished by Tahasildar.
Further he deposed that he had obtained specimen signature of CW-2.
Later accused appeared before him with anticipatory bail and after enquiry he enlarged him on bail.

On 27.07.2016, Sagar hospital issued letter along with medical bill and discharge summary of patient under IP No.0131721 for reference and medical records submitted by accused and medical records submitted by hospital were not tallying.
Later on 15.08.2016, he had obtained specimen signature hand writings of A1 & 2 and on 22.08.2016, he issued notice to Malya hospital seeking information about employees details.
Accordingly, they furnished the same.
Thereafter he recorded further statement of CW-10 & 11 and other witnesses.
Further on 27.10.2016, he sent sample sign and hand writing for expert examination and submitted charge sheet.
13. Further prosecution examined CW-12 as PW-7.
He being the Doctor deposed that he never worked at Sagar hospital and signature appearing in Ex.P.7 and 8 not belongs to him.

Accordingly,
he has given his statement to IO.
14. Further prosecution examined CW-16 as PW-8.
He being one of the Police Official deposed that he handed over the file to CW-17 for further investigation.
15. Further prosecution examined CW-13 as PW-9.

He being administrative at Malya hospital deposed that as per the request made by the IO he has furnished Ex.P.16 to 17.
16.

By relying on above said oral and documentary evidence led by the prosecution learned Snr.APP vehemently argued that accused No.1 & 2 by colluding with each other have created fake medical bills in the name of Sagar hospital thereafter by giving false IP Number as if CW-2 had taken treatment at Sagar hospital and applied for the CM Relief Fund in the name of CW-2.
Thereby he sought to convict the accused.

17. Further in the present case accused have taken various defences and contended that at no point of time they had applied for CM Relief Fund on behalf of CW-2 and they have not committed any offence as alleged by the prosecution.
In order to substantiate the same the counsel for the accused has relied upon chief examination of PW-1 who is seizure mahazar witness as per Ex.P.7.

On perusal of the same he specifically deposed that "police have not accompanied accused persons to the Sagar clinic and he also deposed that police have not informed about involvement of the accused in this case".
Further the counsel for the accused contended that in the Sagar clinic there is no facility for admission.

In order to substantiate the same he relied upon the cross examination of PW-1 in which he stated that "It is true to suggest that whatever the bills to be made by Sagar hospital it will be done in the Sagar hospital only but not in the Sagar clinic.
It is true to suggest that the accused was working in Sagar clinic but not in Sagar hospital".
However in the present case the police have conducted mahazar at Sagar clinic".
Further the counsel for the accused relied upon the evidence of PW-2 who not supported the case of the prosecution and turned hostile though Snr.

18. The prosecution claimed that A1 is employee at Sagar hospital but PW-4 in his cross examination specifically stated that " 
  
 
             

  
 

  
 
  

 ".

19. Further learned counsel for the accused vehemently argued that in order to bring home the guilt of the accused for the offence of forgery there shall be some expert evidence to corroborate the same.
But on perusal of the materials on record in the present case though IO has contended that disputed and admitted specimen hand writing and signature were sent to FSL.
However the expert who examined the documents neither examined nor his report adduced in his evidence.
Further the CW-1/PW-3 not turned back and led his evidence and his evidence also discarded.

Therefore in order to bring home the guilt of the accused for the offence of 468 the prosecution has to prove that the contents application made for CM Relief was filled by accused and signature appearing said application were forged by accused persons.
No doubt the prosecution has examined authors of said application but they simply denied the signature appearing on those documents.
20. In order to corroborate the same and in order to establish that though signatures and hand writings were of accused the prosecution has not adduced any expert evidence.

In the absence of such material evidence it is difficult to believe the version of the prosecution and it is settled criminal jurisprudence the prosecution has to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
However in this case prosecution utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence point No.1 is answered in the Negative.

21. Point No.2: - For the reasons stated and findings given on point No.1, following is:
ORDER
Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 & 2 are acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471, 420, 511, 201 r/w 34 of IPC.

The bail bond and surety bond executed by accused No.1 & 2 shall continue for a period of two months from the date of this order and thereafter same shall stand canceled automatically.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, typed by her directly on computer, revised, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 16 th day of April, 2024).
